# Device Claims Review: Consumer Web Page

**Reviewed:** 2024-05-22
**Device / IVD:** Home blood-pressure monitor — Class IIa
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Publikum (ungated consumer web page)
**Markets:** DE (Germany)

## Summary

2 claims reviewed. 1 reword, 1 OK.

**Ready to publish:** No — rewrite needed.

---

## Findings

**Claim:** "Don't gamble with your heart — check your pressure daily."
**Breach:** HWG § 11(1) no. 7
**Why:** The phrasing "Don't gamble with your heart" suggests that health is at risk or impaired by the *non-use* of the device. This "fear-of-not-using" framing is explicitly prohibited for devices in consumer-facing advertising.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(b) — if the "don't gamble" framing implies a preventative clinical benefit the device (a monitor) does not deliver.
**Call:** Reword
**Suggested fix:** "Monitor your heart health — check your pressure daily."

**Claim:** "Recommended by Professor Schmidt, cardiologist."
**Breach:** none
**Why:** While professional endorsements are banned for medicinal products, HWG § 11(1) only applies nos. 7, 8, 9, 11, and 12 to medical devices. Item no. 2 (professional endorsements) is omitted, meaning they are permissible for devices if true.
**Evidence needed:** Documentation confirming the identity, credentials, and actual recommendation of Professor Schmidt.
**Also engaged:** HWG § 3 no. 3(b), UWG § 5(2) no. 3 — if the person is fictional or the credentials (cardiologist) are inaccurate.
**Call:** OK (Verify)
**Suggested fix:** [Keep as is, provided substantiation is in the technical file.]

---

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "Recommended by Professor Schmidt..." | Signed testimonial and proof of medical registration (cardiology) | Clinical/Legal |
| "check your pressure daily" | Confirmation that daily frequency is within the assessed intended purpose and IFU | Clinical/RA |

---

## Provisions cited

- **MDR Art. 7(b)** [verified]
- **HWG § 11(1) no. 7** [verified]
- **HWG § 3 no. 3(b)** [verified]
- **UWG § 5(2) no. 3** [verified]

---

## Limits

This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht oder Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

> Limb (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is **not assessed**: I have not seen the intended purpose. It is the limb device marketing trips most often, so paste it from the technical documentation or DoC and I will cover it. Everything above reviews limbs (a), (b) and (c).
